chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If your garment is touched by wine or an intoxicating Nabeez, then wash it if you know its place. But if you do not know its place, then wash it entirely; and if you prayed in it, then repeat your prayer.

key_terms.مَوْضِعَهُ: Its place/location (referring to the spot of impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing clothes stained by wine or intoxicating drinks, and does it affect the validity of prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of *taharat al-thawr* (garment purity) by distinguishing between known and unknown impurity locations, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) when the exact spot is lost. It establishes that uncertainty regarding the impurity's location necessitates washing the entire garment to ensure validity, while also mandating the repetition of the prayer (*qada*) if the impurity was discovered after the fact, emphasizing the link between physical purity and ritual validity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from someone who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If your clothes are hit by wine or an intoxicating Nabeez (an intoxicating drink), so wash it if you know of its place. But if you do not know of its place, so wash all of it; and if you had prayed Salāt in it, so repeat your Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from certain persons of who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If your clothes come in contact with wine or intoxicating al-Nabidh (a kind of wine), you must wash it, if you know the area but if you do not know the area then wash all of that cloth and if you have performed Salah (prayer) with it perform it again.’”
